system:
You write the final report of a trial-autopsy system for an analyst. Plain language, precise,
no hype. Use only the provided material; every number must appear in it. When you name the source of a number,
use the source title given for that fact_id in the Facts list. State uncertainty honestly.

Return JSON only:
{"headline": "<one sentence verdict>",
 "summary": "<3-5 sentences: what happened or is expected, why, how sure>",
 "key_evidence": ["<short bullet with the number and its source title>", "..."],
 "what_would_change_this": "<one or two sentences>",
 "readthrough_note": "<one or two sentences on other programmes, or empty>"}

Case: AURORA NCT00240331 - AURORA: Crestor 10mg Versus Placebo in Subjects With End-stage Renal Disease (ESRD) | mode: autopsy | as_of: 2009-03-30
Drug: rosuvastatin (HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor)

Verdict: {"outcome": "failure", "outcome_basis": "readout: \"Patients receiving hemodialysis for treatment of end stage renal disease did not benefit from statin therapy in the AURORA study\" (announcement:aurora)", "predicted_outcome": "success", "consistency": "calculator expected success with 77% probability; the actual result falls in the remaining 23%", "primary_category": "population", "secondary_categories": ["design_or_endpoint"], "calculator_category": "narrow_success", "confidence": "high", "verification": "done", "probability_of_success": 0.773, "weakest_link": "target genetics: uncertain"}
Calculator: {"case_id": "aurora", "ldl_equivalent_mmol": 0.9, "basis": "LDL-C", "time_factor": 0.854, "expected_hr": 0.826, "causal_rrr": 0.174, "bp_factor": 1.0, "power": 0.773, "mde_hr_80": 0.821, "outcome": "success", "category": "narrow_success", "secondary": [], "weakest_link": "target genetics: uncertain", "consistent_with_observed": null, "assumptions": ["LDL-C: no baseline given, assumed 2.0"], "notes": []}
Hypotheses: {"hypotheses": [{"category": "population", "status": "supported", "for": [{"text": "AURORA enrolled ESRD patients on chronic hemodialysis (aged 50-80, dialysis ≥3 months), a population where cardiovascular events are driven largely by non-atherosclerotic processes (uremic cardiomyopathy, arrhythmia/sudden death, vascular calcification, volume overload) rather than LDL-driven plaque rupture. The primary endpoint (CV death, nonfatal stroke, nonfatal MI) includes sudden cardiac death and heart failure deaths that LDL lowering does not prevent.", "refs": ["f_7383925506be99", "f_114a306b671b29", "f_e3a74522bb8b7d"]}, {"text": "The calculator predicted HR 0.826 (77% power, MDE 0.821) based on a -45% LDL-C reduction from the CORONA trial (heart failure population), but the observed result was null (p=0.59, HR ~1.0). The 804 total events provided adequate power to detect the predicted effect, yet the observed effect excludes the prediction, indicating the LDL-C reduction did not translate to benefit in this specific population.", "refs": ["calculator", "f_9353f8733ad3dd", "f_9d4bc6d9320487", "f_a75061c6f3526a", "f_fccd28530bc97f"]}], "against": [{"text": "No AURORA-specific LDL-C change or baseline LDL-C data are available in verified facts to confirm the biomarker was moved as expected in this population; the calculator used CORONA trial data as a surrogate.", "refs": ["f_fccd28530bc97f", "calculator"]}], "would_settle": "AURORA on-treatment LDL-C levels and cause-specific mortality breakdown (sudden death vs. MI vs. stroke) to confirm event types not preventable by LDL lowering."}, {"category": "biomarker_not_causal", "status": "weakened", "for": [{"text": "The trial showed null result despite calculator predicting benefit from LDL-C lowering, suggesting LDL-C may not be causal for the composite endpoint in ESRD.", "refs": ["calculator", "f_e3a74522bb8b7d", "f_a75061c6f3526a"]}], "against": [{"text": "LDL-C is well-established as causal for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease in the general population via Mendelian randomization and statin trials; the failure here is more likely due to the population's distinct pathophysiology (non-atherosclerotic events) than LDL-C being non-causal per se.", "refs": ["f_371d4f07f55da0"]}, {"text": "The calculator's 'narrow_success' prediction assumed the CTT meta-analysis relationship (LDL-C reduction → CV benefit) applies universally, but this relationship derives from populations with predominantly atherosclerotic events.", "refs": ["calculator"]}], "would_settle": "Genetic evidence specific to ESRD populations or mediation analysis showing LDL-C reduction does not mediate benefit in dialysis patients."}, {"category": "design_or_endpoint", "status": "supported", "for": [{"text": "The primary endpoint composite (CV death, nonfatal stroke, nonfatal MI) includes cardiovascular death, which in hemodialysis patients is predominantly sudden cardiac death/arrhythmia and heart failure death — events not prevented by LDL lowering. This dilutes any benefit on atherosclerotic events (MI, stroke).", "refs": ["f_114a306b671b29", "f_7383925506be99"]}, {"text": "Median follow-up of 3.8 years is adequate for atherosclerotic event reduction (per CTT), but if the dominant events are non-atherosclerotic, longer follow-up would not help.", "refs": ["f_0d92f6cffd0e4a", "calculator"]}], "against": [{"text": "The endpoint is standard for CV outcome trials and was also used in CORONA (which was also neutral). The design did not have active comparator or crossover issues.", "refs": ["f_24ce8f50cdc331", "f_dfb89c14bedb9f"]}], "would_settle": "Cause-specific mortality data from AURORA showing proportion of CV deaths that are sudden/arrhythmic vs. atherosclerotic."}, {"category": "effect_too_small", "status": "weakened", "for": [{"text": "The calculator predicted HR 0.826 with 77% power and MDE 0.821, meaning the trial was sized to detect the expected effect.", "refs": ["calculator"]}], "against": [{"text": "Observed HR ~1.0 (p=0.59) with 804 events yields a 95% CI approximately 0.84-1.12, which excludes the predicted HR 0.826. The effect is not merely too small to detect — it is absent.", "refs": ["f_a75061c6f3526a", "f_9353f8733ad3dd", "f_9d4bc6d9320487", "calculator"]}], "would_settle": "Not applicable — the data already exclude a too-small effect."}, {"category": "target_not_causal", "status": "weakened", "for": [{"text": "HMGCR genetic association score 0.695 for coronary artery disorder, but evidence_before_cutoff=0 (all 4 genetic evidence items published after 2009-03-30 cutoff).", "refs": ["f_371d4f07f55da0"]}], "against": [{"text": "HMGCR is the target of all statins, which have robust CV benefit in numerous trials in non-ESRD populations. The target is causal in general; the issue is population-specific.", "refs": ["f_9ece69e63dc277", "f_fa6480d6d7619d"]}], "would_settle": "Pre-cutoff genetic evidence for HMGCR and coronary disease (not available at as_of date)."}, {"category": "off_target_harm", "status": "weakened", "for": [], "against": [{"text": "Safety signal: 'number of patients reporting adverse events was similar in both the rosuvastatin and placebo groups' (AURORA). No off-target harm signal to offset benefit.", "refs": ["f_48035d202aa3e8"]}, {"text": "No blood pressure increase or other harm biomarker changes reported.", "refs": ["calculator"]}], "would_settle": "Not applicable — no evidence of harm."}, {"category": "execution_or_nonscientific", "status": "weakened", "for": [], "against": [{"text": "Trial completed as planned (not stopped early), 2750-2776 randomized, 804 events accrued, median follow-up 3.8 years. Adherence and execution appear adequate.", "refs": ["f_b6ff001d3294d1", "f_e13f24dde6c1e0", "f_0d92f6cffd0e4a", "f_dfb89c14bedb9f"]}], "would_settle": "Not applicable — trial executed properly."}, {"category": "insufficient_data", "status": "weakened", "for": [{"text": "No AURORA-specific LDL-C baseline or on-treatment values in verified facts; calculator assumed 2.0 mmol/L baseline and used CORONA trial -45% change as surrogate.", "refs": ["calculator", "f_fccd28530bc97f"]}], "against": [{"text": "Key trial results (events, p-value, follow-up, population, endpoint, readout) are available from the announcement. The null result is clear and the main explanations (population, endpoint) can be assessed without the missing LDL-C data.", "refs": ["f_9353f8733ad3dd", "f_9d4bc6d9320487", "f_a75061c6f3526a", "f_e3a74522bb8b7d", "f_7383925506be99", "f_114a306b671b29"]}], "would_settle": "AURORA lipid substudy data (if any) confirming LDL-C reduction magnitude in ESRD."}], "primary_category": "population", "secondary_categories": ["design_or_endpoint"], "confidence": "high", "departure_from_calculator": "Calculator categorized as 'narrow_success' (predicted HR 0.826, 77% power, MDE 0.821) but the trial result was null (p=0.59, HR ~1.0). The departure is explained by the population-specific pathophysiology: in ESRD on hemodialysis, the composite endpoint events are driven largely by non-atherosclerotic processes (sudden death, heart failure, vascular calcification) that LDL lowering does not prevent, so the expected benefit from LDL-C reduction does not apply. This is a 'population' explanation, not a failure of the biomarker or target in general."}
